relevance.rationale: The folio's proved per-partition binding weight is Delta_lambda = (-1)^{n(lambda)} dim V_lambda and is described in prose as 'the signed Springer dimension' (mba-sidecar-delta-lambda-closure.md, mba-step09b, two-row-stratum.md), but no Springer reference exists anywhere in folio/schema/references.ts — the only 'Springer' hits are the publisher. §2 of this survey is a compact, citable statement of the Springer correspondence for GL_n, which is the naming's actual backing. The bulk of the survey — generalised Springer correspondence, exotic symmetric spaces for Sp/SO, double Kostka polynomials — has no QOU consumer I can name; the folio's type-B material is the Kashiwara folded-crystal apparatus, a different construction, and I did not verify any link. Corpus-grep of docs/audits, content/, computations/ for Springer-correspondence backing: none found.

keyResults.statement: For the Springer resolution of the unipotent variety of GL_n, the top cohomology H^{2d_x}(B_x) of the Springer fibre B_x = pi^{-1}(x) carries an irreducible S_n-action, and for x in the class O_lambda one has H^{2d_x}(B_x) ≅ V_lambda, giving the bijection between unipotent classes and Irr(S_n).
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the citation for calling Delta_lambda a 'signed Springer dimension': the magnitude dim V_lambda is the top-cohomology dimension of the Springer fibre and the sign exponent is that fibre's dimension d_x, which in type A is n(lambda) up to the standard transpose convention. Flag rather than assume that convention — the folio should record which of n(lambda)/n(lambda') its d_x matches before leaning on the identification.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan; the folio's 'signed Springer dimension' terminology has no Springer citation at all.
mba-sidecar-delta-lambda-closure names the signed Springer dimension in an algorithm block with no source; Thm 2.1(iv) is the statement being invoked.

The transpose convention for d_x = dim B_x vs n(lambda) is not settled in the folio and the proved Lean value depends on which one is meant; record the convention check rather than silently asserting the identification. Explicitly not aid-proof — the Lean theorem is already proved by other means and this citation does not enter its proof.
